the proposed method for annotation of paintings with high semantic concepts using the transductive inference and disambiguation framework outperforms the conventional methods and is suitable for the annotation of large image collections.
the proposed method of combining the transductive inference with ontology-based concept dis-ambiguation generates high-quality image-level annotation for paintings.

the transductive inference method with the use of visual concepts out-performs the baseline methods, the ontology-based concept-disambiguation method improves the annotation results and that the proposed framework is useful for annotating high semantic concepts for paintings.
In summary, our research is concerned with

1) the use of high-level semantic concepts in annotation and retrieval of paintings, 2) the use of transductive inference framework for annotation of high-level semantic features, and 3) the use of ontology-based concept dis-ambiguation to generate global annotation of images.

a) the development of the ontology of visual-level and high-level artistic concepts, b) the annotation of high-level concepts with the transductive inference and the disambiguation of conflicting assignments, and c) the flexible retrieval of paintings using the annotated high-level concepts.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of the visual-level concepts, combined with the transductive inference and the disambiguation framework, significantly improves the performance of annotating high-level semantic concepts to paintings.
the proposed framework and the ontology-based disambiguating method are useful in the context of annotation of high-level concepts to paintings and can be used for flexible image retrieval.
our approach to annotation of paintings using transductive inference is a novel and promising approach for annotating paintings with semantic concepts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed framework for annotating highlevel concepts with visual-level concepts as cues is highly effective in generating the high-level annotations and is robust for several annotation scenarios.

a) we propose a novel framework for annotating paintings with high-level concepts using transductive learning; b) we propose a method for resolving conflicting assignments of concepts using the domain knowledge represented as a concept ontology and c) we demonstrate that our framework and the proposed disambiguation approach significantly out-perform the state-of-the-art methods for the annotation of paintings.

the combination of low-level features and domain-specific concepts improves the annotation performance and that the ontology-based disambigation method can resolve conflicting annotations and improve the overall annotation accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the domain-specific knowledge is crucial for accurate annotation and flexible retrieval.
the use of visual concepts in conjunction with the ontology-based disambiguations leads to improved performance in the task of annotating high-level semantic concepts.
the domain knowledge can be effectively incorporated to improve the accuracy of high-level annotation of images.
